scope: Local source, schema, unit, tenant/API, loopback OTLP/HTTP protobuf, and fresh restricted-role PostgreSQL 17.10 evidence for extending authenticated trace-context propagation to every current shared durable-envelope type. No production, staging, provider sandbox, external collector, or customer data was used.

priorEvidence.purpose: Accepted ADR 0036 schema, canonical job-hash binding, authority-before-parent worker contract, reconciliation producer, and two-span loopback trace evidence.

decision.reasonNoNewAdr: ADR 0036 explicitly permits other durable producers to adopt the optional field when they capture local context and preserve authority-before-parent ordering.

producerContract.captureSource: activeTraceparent() from the currently active locally accepted API or authorized worker consumer span
producerContract.providerWebhookAuthorizationBoundary: The local context is passed into the service, but the immutable receipt and outbox are written only after exact provider-signature verification and tenant-bound connection authority resolution.
producerContract.csvCommitAuthorizationBoundary: Tenant permission is resolved before locally accepted context reaches the commit service and tenant transaction.
producerContract.userProviderSyncAuthorizationBoundary: Tenant permission and exact organization confirmation are resolved before locally accepted context reaches the sync manager and tenant transaction.
producerContract.reconciliationAuthorizationBoundary: Existing tenant-authorized ADR 0036 producer remains unchanged.
producerContract.nestedProviderSyncBoundary: After the sync queue envelope is authorized against PostgreSQL and its consumer span is active, the worker captures that local span for each child connector.webhook.received envelope.
producerContract.scheduledProviderSyncRoot: provider-gap-repair-scheduler requests intentionally omit traceContext because no authenticated API request exists; child item jobs can continue from the active authorized sync-consumer span.

limitations: The loopback OTLP test runs one process-global SDK and reconstructs API, durable consumer, and nested durable consumer spans directly. It proves context semantics, not a deployed API/outbox/Redis/worker/collector multi-process trace.

The fresh PostgreSQL exercise verifies exact immutable outbox payloads and restricted application/worker behavior but does not run Redis, BullMQ, an independent API process, or an independent worker process.

The disposable database used loopback host trust for test orchestration. Role capability, tenant transactions, forced RLS, and offline checksums were exercised, but this is not production transport/authentication evidence.
Provider webhook and sync behavior used synthetic signed fixtures and page sources. No authorized Shopify or Stripe sandbox was accessed.
Scheduled provider-sync requests intentionally have no authenticated request parent and start roots. Existing envelopes without traceContext also remain valid roots for rolling compatibility.

No protected collector/backend, authentication/egress, retention/access policy, trace search, representative load, collector outage, termination, dashboard, alert, notification, acknowledgement, or on-call response was exercised.
Trace context intentionally contains no tenant, customer, payment, job, credential, or financial data. Operators must use separately protected correlation and tenant-authorized evidence.
Telemetry remains bounded and lossy. Missing context or export failure starts or breaks a trace but cannot alter financial work, durable identity, retries, approval, or source-system state.
claim: All current shared durable-envelope producers locally satisfy the authenticated versioned trace-context contract with authority-before-parent worker handling. This is local contract evidence, not production readiness, staging compatibility, provider connectivity, an SLO, or an exercised operational alert path.
